To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have extended the applicability of the density-dependent interaction for the calculation of symmetric nuclear and neutron matter to higher densities; 2) we have shown that the use of the correlated average is not necessary to obtain a realistic equation of state; 3) we have shown the importance of the inclusion of the three-nucleon interaction for the description of nuclear matter; and 4) the use of a density-dependent force is a viable approach for the description of the equation of state

(i) we have developed a consistent method to include the effects of three-nucleon forces into a Green's function approach to nuclear matter and (ii) our results show that the inclusion of correlations in the construction of an in-medium average for the three-body interaction does not introduce significant changes to the nuclear matter energy

(i) the inclusion of three-body forces is crucial for a quantitative description of nuclear matter, (ii) the inclusion of correlations in the construction of density-dependent two-body forces is important for quantitative calculations, (iii) the use of the ladder approximation is crucial for a correct description of bulk properties and (iv) the use of a density-dependent chiral two-body force provides a very good description of the properties of nuclear matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of an effective nuclear force that is based on the chiral effective field theory.
the construction of a consistent and accurate three-body force that can be used in the calculation of the properties of nuclear matter.
the construction of a consistent and reliable many-body approach for the calculation of infinite-matter properties, which can be used as a reference for nuclear structure calculations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density-dependent chiral two-body forces are a good approximation to the underlying many-body problem.
the density dependence of the chiral forces is not crucial for the properties of nuclear matter.
the density dependent force is not able to describe the saturation of nuclear matter and that it is not able to reproduce the empirical saturation point.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of the density-dependent chiral two-body force leads to a significant softening of symmetric nuclear matter.

, within a self-consistent Green’s function approach, the inclusion of the three-body force in a density dependent two-body interaction does not significantly alter the bulk properties of infinite nuclear matter.
the three-body force effects in symmetric nuclear matter are rather small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of the three-body force in the density-dependent interaction is important for the calculation of symmetric nuclear matter at low densities.

the density dependence of the force is crucial in the description of the properties of symmetric nuclear matter, and that the inclusion of three-body forces is important for a correct description of the equation of state at high densities.
the inclusion of the three-body force is crucial for the description of the saturation properties of nuclear matter.
